notes: Difficulty 6 (hardest of the corpus-v1 additions): the naive part - an arm with a flat underside - builds, passes an envelope check and fails printability with a 90 deg overhang finding over 707 mm^2, so the task cannot be passed without modelling the ramp. Acceptance is independent of the run's own reading: the grader re-runs the whole fdm pack on a probed secure backend and requires all three rule ids clean, while the CHECKS pin the envelope, genus 1 (the bore still exists) and the exact ramped volume (a flat-bottomed arm is 10800 mm^3 heavier). The bore is deliberately vertical: a horizontal bore's own crown is a 90 deg unsupported face, which would make the overhang rule unsatisfiable. The reference solution is a file overlay, so its call path is counted by hand: 16 calls (read_globals, write_part, build_part, run_dfm, two edit/build iterations, measure, run_checks); budget 26 leaves ~60% headroom.
